# RGC Public Assets

> The Really Good Culture brand asset library: logos, icons, motifs, 3D brand
> objects, deck artwork, product screens and site imagery. 936 files, exported
> from the master Figma file and served over a CDN.
>
> Repository: https://github.com/RGC-LABS/rgc-public-assets

---

## The one rule: never link to a branch

**Every url you emit must contain a 40-character commit SHA. Never `main`.**

```
NO   https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/RGC-LABS/rgc-public-assets@main/logos/rgc-mark.png
NO   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RGC-LABS/rgc-public-assets/main/logos/rgc-mark.png
NO   https://github.com/RGC-LABS/rgc-public-assets/blob/main/logos/rgc-mark.png

YES  https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/RGC-LABS/rgc-public-assets@ddca2140c761325059910102672b5b3c2f778661/logos/rgc-mark.png
```

`main` is a moving pointer. A deck, a landing page or a generated document that
links to `main` renders correctly today and silently breaks — wrong crop, wrong
logo lockup, or a 404 — the first time someone re-exports that asset. A commit
SHA is immutable: the bytes behind it can never change. Pin once, and the thing
you shipped keeps looking the way you shipped it, forever.

This is not a style preference. Rewriting a pinned url to point at a branch is a
defect. If you are tempted to "clean up" a long url by shortening it to `main`,
don't.

## How to resolve an asset

1. Fetch the manifest:
   `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RGC-LABS/rgc-public-assets/main/assets.json`
2. Find the entry whose `path` you want.
3. Use its `url` **verbatim**. It is already pinned.

The manifest is the *only* thing you fetch from `main` — it is the mutable entry
point, deliberately, so you always discover the current set of assets. Every url
it hands back is immutable. Resolve fresh, embed pinned.

An entry looks like this:

```json
{
  "path": "logos/rgc-logo.svg",
  "category": "logos",
  "bytes": 24321,
  "dimensions": "711x306",
  "content_id": "54aa97ec3d3368cab2def51411053af531d8a16e",
  "commit": "ddca2140c761325059910102672b5b3c2f778661",
  "modified": "2026-08-26T16:33:51+03:00",
  "author": "Criss Moldovan",
  "url": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/RGC-LABS/rgc-public-assets@ddca21.../logos/rgc-logo.svg",
  "url_raw": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RGC-LABS/rgc-public-assets/ddca21.../logos/rgc-logo.svg"
}
```

- `url` — jsDelivr. Use this. Served `cache-control: max-age=31536000, immutable`.
- `url_raw` — same commit via raw.githubusercontent. Fallback only: it is served
  `max-age=300` and is not intended to carry production traffic.
- `commit` — the commit that last modified *this file*, not the repo HEAD. So an
  asset's url only changes when the asset itself changes, and an unchanged file
  keeps one stable url (and one warm CDN entry) across every release.
- `content_id` — the git blob SHA. Identical bytes produce an identical
  `content_id`, so you can tell a genuine re-export from a no-op touch.
- `modified` / `author` — provenance, straight from git history.

## Checking whether your pins are stale

Re-fetch the manifest and compare `content_id` against what you stored. If it is
unchanged, the asset is byte-identical and your existing pinned url is still
correct — do nothing. If it changed, the asset was genuinely re-exported: review
the new version, then update the pin deliberately. Never auto-follow.

## Categories

| Folder | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `logos/` | RGC marks and product marks. `rgc-logo.svg` is the only vector logo. |
| `icons/` | report-icons (156, dark/light pairs), mono (78, `currentColor`), the seven dimension modules, 10 shopper archetypes. |
| `motifs/` | 3D brand objects for dark panels, plus the three 3D product marks. |
| `image-fills/` | Source bitmaps embedded in the Figma file, original resolution. |
| `backgrounds-extras/` | Backgrounds and unmapped layer renders kept from Figma. |
| `deck/` | The 45-section master pitch, 34 blank slide templates, brand-pitch examples. |
| `screens/` | The 10 built product screens. |
| `boards/` | One PNG per Figma branding board. |
| `site/` | Site imagery: site-assets, article headers, LinkedIn sizes. |

Human-readable catalogue with dimensions and sizes: `ASSET-INDEX.md`.

## Brand rules

- **Logos are placed, never redrawn.** Do not recreate a mark in CSS, SVG paths
  or ASCII, do not recolour it, do not rebuild a lockup from parts. Reference the
  file.
- **Every figure in example artwork is illustrative.** Numbers, charts and
  personas inside deck and screen images are examples, not data. Never cite them
  as fact or present them as real results.
- `mono/` icons inherit `currentColor`; report-icons ship as explicit dark/light
  pairs — pick the pair that matches the surface, do not filter one into the other.

## Regenerating

`ASSET-INDEX.md` and `assets.json` are generated. After adding or re-exporting
any asset, commit it first (pinning reads git history), then:

```
python3 tools/build-asset-index.py .
```

The script refuses to emit an unpinned url, and warns about any file not yet
committed.
